Read via jq/node rather than manual scroll: verified top-level shape, verified all 1024 proofs have exactly 10 sibling hashes (well-formed 0x + 64 hex chars) and 10 sibling sums (decimal strings) with zero malformed entries, and confirmed root.sum (1500) equals the sum of the 5 populated entries (100+200+300+400+500). Then ran the real test suite (node --test) which re-derives the whole tree from tooling/payout/canonical-merkle-sum.mjs and deep-equals every one of the 1024 leaves/proofs plus the manifest bytes/digest and orderedProofsDigest against this exact file -- all 4 tests passed. This is a stronger check of full-file correctness than manual line-reading would have been.
purpose: A depth-10, width-1024 canonical Merkle-sum tree used to commit one payout distribution (which HKMN/USDG amount goes to which recipient after a Collector Crypt cycle's proceeds return to the hook) as a single on-chain root (hash+sum), plus a pull-based settlement contract that lets anyone pay any committed recipient once, permissionlessly, against a Merkle-sum proof, funded by an accounting ledger that enforces funded = paid + unpaid at all times.

CanonicalMerkleSum.sol (library, interna: manifestBytes(chainId,hook,cycleId,payoutId,snapshotNumber,snapshotHash,ManifestEntry[]) pure returns bytes -- ABI-encodes+validates the offchain manifest
constants TREE_DEPTH=10, TREE_WIDTH=1024, SCHEMA_VERSION=1, 4 domain-separation tag hashes
errors: InvalidIndex, InvalidRecipient, InvalidAmount, InvalidDirectBalance, EntriesNotStrictlyIncreasing, SumOverflow
PayoutCommitment.sol (abstract, extends: external fundPayoutFromPegCycle(IPegCycleVault.PayoutAuthorization) moneyPath returns PayoutRecord -- one-shot: consumes a vault authorization, requires the hook's USDG balance to have increased by exactly authorization.rootSum, stores the record, credits payoutLiability, requires solvency, emits PayoutFunded
internal _readPayout, internal _consumePayoutEntitlement(payoutId,amount) -- moves amount unpaid->paid and debits the liability ledger
HolderSettlement.sol (abstract, extends: external payEntitlement(payoutId,index,recipient,amount,siblingHashes[10],siblingSums[10]) moneyPath -- NO access control / no msg.sender check: anyone can call this to pay any not-yet-paid, proof-valid entitlement to the recipient named in the proof; marks paid, consumes liability, transfers USDG, requires solvency, emits EntitlementPaid
tooling/payout/canonical-merkle-sum.mjs: keccak256(bytes) -- hand-rolled Keccak-f[1600] (RATE_BYTES=136, standard 0x01/0x80 padding), no external crypto lib

manifestBytes/nonemptyLeaf/emptyLeaf/parentNode/verifyProof/orderedProofsDigest/buildDistribution -- JS mirror of the Solidity library plus tree-building and proof-generation helpers not present onchain
canonicalVector() / writeCanonicalVector(path) -- generates the fixture in test-vectors/payout/canonical-merkle-sum-v1.json; also runnable as a CLI: `node canonical-merkle-sum.mjs OUTPUT_PATH`

invariants: funded = paid + unpaid: enforced arithmetically (unpaidTotal -= amount; paidTotal += amount on every consume) and only ever initialized once per payoutId (paidTotal=0, unpaidTotal=rootSum) at funding time.
One-payment-per-leaf: paidEntitlements[payoutId][index] boolean, set true before the external transfer (checks-effects-interactions), independent of who calls payEntitlement.

Balance-delta binding at funding time: fundPayoutFromPegCycle requires hookBalanceAfter-hookBalanceBefore == authorization.rootSum exactly (not >=), reverting PayoutBalanceDeltaMismatch otherwise -- this is the only onchain check that ties the committed rootSum to real incoming USDG.
Global solvency: _requireSolvent() (hook USDG balance >= sum of all liabilities: programmable+treasury+process+payout) is called after crediting a new payout and after every entitlement payment.
Domain separation: 4 distinct keccak256(name-string) tags (manifest/nonemptyLeaf/emptyLeaf/node) prevent cross-type or cross-level hash collisions/second-preimage games.

Sum binding: every parent node's hash preimage includes both children's (hash,sum) pairs, so a proof cannot supply an inconsistent sibling sum without also changing the resulting hash chain (SumOverflow guarded with a subtraction-based check, not addition-overflow).

Strict leaf ordering in the offchain manifest: entries must be strictly increasing by index (both Solidity _validateEntries and JS validateEntries), and index<1024, recipient nonzero and != hook, amount>0, directBalance>0.

Global moneyPath reentrancy guard (in FeeAccounting.sol, inherited): a single boolean blocks reentry into ANY money-path function while one is executing, not just self-reentry -- fundPayoutFromPegCycle and payEntitlement both use it.

Fee split constants live in FeeAccounting.sol (not in the requested file list but load-bearing for solvency): TOTAL_FEE_BPS=300, PROGRAMMABLE_FEE_BPS=10, TREASURY_FEE_BPS=40, processFee=totalFee-programmableFee-treasuryFee=250bps. This matches the owner-approved repo split (0.10% Programmable + 0.40% treasury + 2.50% process budget = 3.00%) and confirms 0.4+0.1=0.5 lines up with the owner's 'separated 0.5%' statement.
stateTransitions: unfunded -> funded: fundPayoutFromPegCycle (once per payoutId, guarded by PayoutAlreadyFunded -- see suspicion about payoutId==bytes32(0))

funded, unpaidTotal>0, paidEntitlements[id][idx]=false -> paidEntitlements[id][idx]=true, unpaidTotal-=amount, paidTotal+=amount, USDG transferred: payEntitlement (idempotent no-op protection via EntitlementAlreadyPaid revert, not silent skip)
No transition exists to reclaim/sweep/expire an unpaid remainder, and no transition ever un-funds or corrects a bad rootHash/rootSum once committed -- a bad manifest is permanent for that payoutId.
externalDependencies: ProcessBudget (packages/contracts/src/process/ProcessBudget.sol) -- PayoutCommitment's base class, not in the read set; supplies constructor wiring and presumably the process-budget spend path.

FeeAccounting.sol (packages/contracts/src/accounting/FeeAccounting.sol) -- read out-of-scope for context: supplies moneyPath, _requireSolvent, _hookUsdgBalance, _transferExactUsdg, _creditPayoutLiability, _debitPayoutLiability, the fee-split constants, and the abstract _usdgBalanceOf/_transferUsdg/_currentTreasuryBeneficiary hooks whose concrete USDG-adapter implementation is explicitly still 'integration-pending' per its own doc comment.

IPegCycleVault (packages/contracts/src/process/IPegCycleVault.sol) -- PayoutCommitment trusts consumePayoutAuthorization() to have validated the PayoutAuthorization (requirementsRevision, cycleId, manifestDigest, rootHash, rootSum, returnReceiptDigest, expiry, nonce, etc.) before returning operationsTrigger; PayoutCommitment itself does not re-derive or check rootHash/manifestDigest validity, only the resulting balance delta.
HookemonHook.sol wires HolderSettlement (and therefore PayoutCommitment/CanonicalMerkleSum) into the concrete deployed hook contract alongside CanonicalMarketCallback and HookemonIssuance.

canonical-merkle-sum.mjs has zero npm dependencies -- it reimplements Keccak-256 from scratch (custom permute/rotateLeft/ROUND_CONSTANTS) rather than using a pinned crypto library; correctness rests entirely on this file's own bit-manipulation code plus the checked-in fixture.

autonomyGaps: Manifest/root authenticity is explicitly out of scope for these contracts: PayoutCommitment.sol's own header doc says 'Manifest publication and independent proof verification remain offchain preflight duties.' fundPayoutFromPegCycle only checks that the USDG balance increased by exactly rootSum; it never reconstructs or spot-checks the Merkle-sum tree from real entries. For a fully unattended 20-minute cycle, whatever offchain service builds the manifest (which holder gets how much) and gets pegCycleVault to authorize it is a single point of failure with no onchain fallback verification -- that service is not present in this file set.

No push/keeper distribution exists here: settlement is strictly pull-based -- someone (a bot, in the fully-autonomous target) must call payEntitlement separately for every one of up to 1024 leaf indices per payout, per cycle, supplying the exact proof. Nothing in PayoutCommitment/HolderSettlement enumerates holders or drives payment automatically; an external keeper/automation component (not among the read files, and per repository facts, still Phase 2 / deferred) is required to actually realize 'proceeds ... distributed pro rata to HKMN holders automatically.'

No sweep/expiry/reclaim path for unpaid remainders: if a holder never claims (e.g., they don't run a bot, or a proof submission is censored/fails), unpaidTotal for that payoutId sits forever with no mechanism in these 3 files to redirect it (e.g., after a timeout) -- relevant for a dashboard that must show 'stuck cycle' status and offer a restart/kick action per the owner's ask, since a stuck *unclaimed* holder payout isn't something these contracts let an operator kick.

Fixed 1024-leaf capacity per payoutId (TREE_WIDTH): if HKMN's holder count for a given pro-rata distribution ever exceeds 1024, a single payoutId/manifest cannot represent it; nothing in these files chunks a large holder set across multiple payoutIds automatically.

The `directBalance` field on each ManifestEntry is validated (must be nonzero) in both Solidity and JS but is never consumed by any comparison/assertion against `amount` anywhere in these files -- if it was meant to enforce some accounting relationship (e.g., paid amount can't exceed a holder's already-custodied balance), that check is not implemented here, which matters for an autonomous system meant to run without manual sanity-checking of each cycle's payout.

USDG token adapter is still integration-pending (FeeAccounting.sol's own header comment): _usdgBalanceOf/_transferUsdg are abstract virtual hooks with no concrete implementation visible in this file set, so the actual funding/payment path cannot be exercised end-to-end from these files alone.

suspicions.note: PayoutAlreadyFunded guard is `if (payouts[authorization.payoutId].payoutId != bytes32(0)) revert PayoutAlreadyFunded();`. This uses the struct's own payoutId field equal to bytes32(0) as the 'slot empty' sentinel. If authorization.payoutId is itself bytes32(0), the stored record's payoutId field is always set to bytes32(0) too (record.payoutId = authorization.payoutId), so the guard condition is permanently false for that key -- fundPayoutFromPegCycle can be called an unlimited number of times for payoutId==bytes32(0), each call overwriting the prior PayoutRecord (resetting paidTotal to 0 and unpaidTotal to the new rootSum) while leftover paidEntitlements[bytes32(0)][index] bits from the previous generation remain permanently 'paid' and block re-claiming those indices under the new record. Whether this is reachable depends on whether IPegCycleVault (out of scope) ever allows payoutId==bytes32(0) to be authorized; nothing in this file itself forbids it.

`_verifyEntitlementProof` hardcodes the tree width as the literal `1024` (`index >= 1024`) instead of referencing `CanonicalMerkleSum.TREE_WIDTH`. Currently correct since TREE_WIDTH==1024, but it is a duplicated magic number that would silently desynchronize from the library if TREE_WIDTH ever changes.

ManifestEntry.directBalance is required to be nonzero (line 170) but is not referenced by any arithmetic check elsewhere in this file or in PayoutCommitment/HolderSettlement -- it only affects manifestDigest (and therefore leaf hashes) indirectly. Purpose and intended invariant unclear from the code alone (see openQuestions).

keccak256 is a from-scratch, ~90-line hand-rolled Keccak-f[1600] implementation with no unit tests of the primitive in isolation (only end-to-end tree/tag outputs are asserted against the fixture in canonical-merkle-sum.test.mjs). If it happened to be subtly wrong in a way that still produced internally self-consistent tree structure (extremely unlikely given padding/rotation constants match the public Keccak spec, but not independently cross-checked here against e.g. Node's built-in crypto or a known keccak256 test vector), the offchain manifest/root would not match what the Solidity keccak256 actually computes on-chain, and every proof built offchain would fail onchain verification. This file has zero external dependencies by design, which is good for supply-chain safety but removes the option of cross-checking against a well-known audited implementation at import time.
